reading.en: You could say modern society has developed with the aim of 'not having to wait'. Things we order arrive the next day, and we can watch films at home right away without going to the cinema. With an app, we instantly know the fastest train connection. We have seen waiting as wasted time and worked hard to reduce it. Not having to wait is certainly nice. But is waiting time really all wasted? When I was a child, my favourite manga magazine came out only once a month. During the month until the next issue, my friends and I talked again and again about what would happen next. I even imagined the next part and drew it. Looking back, that month was as much fun as the manga itself. Waiting leaves room for imagination. Because answers are not given right away, people think for themselves and build up their hopes. And what we get after waiting feels more precious than what we get at once. Of course, some waiting, like long waits at hospitals or for paperwork at city offices, should be reduced. I don't mean we should enjoy all waiting. What I want to say is: in our pursuit of convenience, are we giving up even the things we gain from waiting? Sometimes, instead of searching for the answer right away, we could try enjoying the time spent waiting.
